title: Killian's boxing gloves and his murder
summary: Neither Barnet nor Willard knows what Killian's miniature boxing gloves meant; Willard describes his murder by a janitor with a death list.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: He's a funny guy. When Killian was in your band did he have those little boxing gloves dangling from his trumpet?
I have no idea. I used to see them there and I always meant to ask him and I never did.
Me too, because he had them when he was with Duke, I know, and --
I don't know what that was for.
Little perfect miniatures dangling from below the trumpet.

He was, for the record, murdered here in an apartment house in Los Angeles, on East 35th Street, by a janitor who had a death list, and on the death list were a great many members of the Ellington band, that apparently
he never got to finish his list.
Yeah. He had everybody, I guess, he'd ever met, because some of the members of the band had stayed in that apartment house, and they discovered that he had a death list.
I had heard that he was out on parole from another murder.

He was. He'd done seven years and they let him out. And at the time he was prosecuted for murdering Al and his girl friend, the District Attorney asked that he be sentenced to life without possibility of parole, and the judge refused, which I never understood. So the man was eligible for parole again. I don't know if he ever got out or not, but --
